Label: ^specific gravity\b|^density\b
Note: a density's specimen form is rarely stated

Label: ^strength\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: a row labelled only "Strength" under a tensile standard states no endpoint, which is the property this is

Label: ^stress at break\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the sheet names the endpoint and the method column names the tensile test; a stress the sheet states at an elongation is not this row and is left for the owner

Label: ^breaking stress\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the same row under the maker’s other name for it

Label: ^yield (stress|strength)\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the method column names the tensile test, so the yield is the tensile one

Label: ^yield strain\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the strain at yield of a tensile test is the elongation at yield

Label: ^e-?modulus\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?178|ASTM\s?D\s?790)\b)
Note: a sheet may head the row with the modulus alone; which modulus it is is the test it names, and ISO 178 is the bending test

Label: ^e-?modulus\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the same row where the test it names is the tensile one

Label: ^(tensile )?elongation[^a-z]{0,3}\(?(at )?break|^tensile strain at break|^tensile elongation[^a-z]*(at )?break|^elongation[^a-z]*at break|^tensile strain \(break\)
^elongation at stren\w*
Note: a sheet spells it strenght; a source’s own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^charpy
Note: an unqualified Charpy row is the unnotched one; the method may say otherwise and wins

Label: ^notched impact strength\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?179|ISO\s?180|ASTM\s?D\s?256|GB\s?/\s?T\s?(?:1043|1843))\b)
Note: the row names the notch and not the test, and the method column names which test it is; a row that names no method is left to the label above it, which is where a sheet that prints a block per notch says Charpy or Izod

Label: ^(temperature of deflection under load|heat (deflection|distortion) temp(erature)?\b|deflection temp(erature)?\b|hdt)
Note: the load is a condition the row or the line above states; a sheet may abbreviate it "Heat deflection temp."

Label: ^(shore|rockwell) hardness|^hardness|^shore [ad]\b
Note: the scale is part of the unit, and the sheet states it

Label: ^contin[uo]*s (service|use|operating) temperature
Note: a sheet spells it Continous; a source's own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^low temperature impact( strength)?
Note: a maker's name for an impact test run below room temperature; which test it is comes from the standard it names, and the temperature is the row's own condition

Label: ^impact\b|^notched$|^unnotched$
Note: the sheet names no test; ISO 180 or ASTM D256 makes it Izod, ISO 179 or GB/T 1043 Charpy

Label: ^tensile elongation\b|^elongation\b|^ultimate elongation\b|^nominal (elongation|strain) at break\b|^strain at break\b
Note: an unqualified ISO 527 elongation is the value at failure, which is how this database records the sheets that print one figure; a sheet that labels its endpoint matches the row above this one
